text: Is polysemanticity in LLM neurons primarily explained by superposition (the model compressing more features than it has dimensions)?

terms.superposition: The model represents more features than it has dimensions, so features share neurons/directions (the Toy Models count definition).
terms.polysemanticity: A single neuron responds to multiple unrelated concepts.
terms.feature: A property of the input that the model represents and downstream computation uses.

text: Do frontier models' chains of thought reliably reveal the factors that actually drive their answers, enough to support CoT monitoring?

terms.faithfulness: The CoT reveals the factors that actually drive the model's answer.
terms.monitorability: The CoT is informative enough for a monitor to catch the behaviour it is looking for.
terms.verbalization: The model explicitly mentions a given factor (e.g. a planted hint) in its CoT.

text: Do frontier LLMs robustly fake alignment (behave differently when they believe they're being trained vs. unmonitored) across models and setups?

terms.alignment faking: Strategically complying during (believed) training in order to preserve preferences that would otherwise be trained away.
terms.training awareness: The model's belief about whether its current outputs will be used for training.
terms.compliance gap: The difference in behaviour between believed-training and believed-unmonitored conditions.
